manual_review.notes: The most frequent model error: attributing the total dose count to a single medication (e.g. 'Fictional Med AW-1 was administered 8 times' when the record shows 6 AW-1 + 2 S-1). Present in 10 of 36 outputs. Benchmark run 20261111-140655 did not detect these; the per-medication check was added after this review, and a false positive it introduced ('8 doses of S-1 and AW-1' = a correct combined total) was found in run 20261111-141959 and fixed with a regression test. The 'no contradicted values' metric therefore dropped between runs because detection improved, not because outputs changed (generation is deterministic at temperature 0).
Invented detail: 'decreased to 3 by release' — P032 has no recorded release. Caught by the release check added after review; sentence replaced with the computed score statement.

Model cited GAP-01 for 'a documentation gap regarding release status' in a 24 h window with no gaps. The fabricated citation was removed and, since it was the sentence's only support, the sentence was dropped.
Mis-citation not detectable by the validator: 'No vital signs were recorded in the last 20.88 h [GAP-01]' is true of the data, but GAP-01 describes missing assessments, not vital signs.

Context loss: 'monitored at least every 4 hours for the first 72 hours [BJA-2023-0102]' comes from the triage table for at-risk individuals who appear well, and was presented as monitoring during withdrawal management. This is the main reason hybrid's guideline citation relevance on patient cases (0.71) trails dense (0.85): BM25 surfaces keyword-similar screening passages. On guideline-only questions hybrid retrieved and cited gold passages more often than dense.

All three methods missed the gold passages for 'How should patients in stimulant withdrawal be monitored?'. They returned stimulant screening/triage monitoring passages instead. The question is ambiguous between pre-treatment and during-treatment monitoring; gold labels were not changed after seeing results.
Citation validity ≥ 98.8% in all configurations. About 9–12% of patient-record sentences carry no citation, mostly the second clause of multi-measure vital-sign sentences.

No severity classification or treatment-recommendation sentences reached the validated output in this run. The earlier development run that classified a CIWA-Ar of 27 as 'moderate range (10–18)' led to the severity-removal rule; it did not recur after the prompt change.
Adding 4 guideline passages raises the prompt from ~3.4k to ~4.8k tokens and mean end-to-end time from ~11 s to ~15 s; retrieval itself is ~25–65 ms.
